findings.title: A creator confession completed as possession and praise

findings.title: Finite writing supplies meet inexhaustible expression
findings.claim: The focus's need-free predicate is refracted by 31:27: even if the lower world and seas become writing supplies, those materials run out before Allah's words, so independence can also be heard as inexhaustibility of expression.
findings.mechanism: Al-Ghaniyy carries freedom from need, and al-arḍ names the lower domain. The next ayah independently turns the earth's trees into pens and the sea into replenishing ink, then states that the supplies exhaust while Allah's words do not. The focus's owned earth thus meets a finite apparatus of expression; the contrast makes the need-free predicate resonate with non-depletion.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the owned world not only as a domain under Allah's possession, but as a finite supply that cannot measure or exhaust what is expressed as His words.
findings.containment: The writing analogy may measure the inexhaustibility of the words without glossing al-Ghaniyy itself; the contextual extension adds to, and does not replace, the focus's ordinary claim of freedom from need. The HFT context roots and indices remain attributed.

findings.title: Kinship does not make one creature sufficient for another
findings.claim: The focus word al-Ghaniyy can resonate with sufficing another or standing in for another in a relational setting; 31:33 denies that exchange in both directions between parent and child, making creaturely sufficiency non-transferable even at the closest bond.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the need-free predicate and the registered branch for being sufficient for another or standing in another's place. The later warning independently repeats parent-child relations and denies that either can answer for the other, down to not even one thing. That reciprocal failure supplies the relation the focus form itself does not state, so its sufficiency branch is tested against the limit of kinship.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees personal need and responsibility remain with each person: the strongest family bond cannot act as a substitute that makes either party sufficient for the other.
findings.containment: The focus word is an attributive predicate, not a local relational construction; the for-another and standing-in facets therefore survive only as contextual resonances. 31:33 may still be read as a juridical warning about accountability, without extending it to a general account of dependence. Its HFT word indices and context-root branches remain attributed.

findings.title: The owned earth and a future no creature can know
findings.claim: 31:34 returns the focus's earth and needlessness as a limit on creaturely command: every self remains within the owned domain but does not know its next gain or even the earth of its death, so possession reaches an endpoint outside human knowledge.
findings.mechanism: The focus assigns the upper and lower domains to Allah and predicates al-Ghaniyy. The closing ayah locates decisive knowledge with Him while twice denying that a self knows what it will gain tomorrow or in which earth it will die. The specific earth of death returns through the focus's own earth word, and the gap between universal possession and a person's unknown future endpoint makes the focus's domain relation extend into temporal and epistemic enclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold both statements together: the earth belongs to Allah, while no person owns the knowledge of where life will end or what tomorrow brings.
findings.containment: 31:34 may remain a list of matters whose knowledge belongs to Allah rather than a gloss of possession. The future-endpoint reading is an attributed extension; the ordinary spatial claim remains fully recoverable, and the exact HFT word/root assignments are not independently verified.

epistemic.reason: The exact text names tomorrow's gain and the earth of death, and the trace returns through the focus's registered earth and needlessness branches. The HFT reader identity and non-focus morphology remain unverified.

findings.title: The upper domain as an ordered circuit
findings.claim: The focus names an upper domain whose motion is made visible in 31:29: night and day enter one another, and the sun and moon run to a specified term, so possession can be seen as an active order with bounded circuits rather than only a static domain.
findings.mechanism: Al-samāwāt carries the upper sky-domain. The following context supplies alternating night and day, running luminaries, an appointed term, and a designation mapped by the HFT to the registered naming branch. Contact among these separate elements makes the upper domain's possession temporal and ordered; the HFT's naming trace returns through the focus's sky word without redefining that word.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can picture the upper domain as a working sequence of interlocking phases and moving bodies, each held to a specified end.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the heavens belong to Allah. The return of the naming branch from 31:29 is source-attributed because target morphology and reader identity are unverified; it does not make samāwāt mean 'name.' The context can also be read as a separate account of cosmic governance.

epistemic.reason: The exact context Arabic names the alternating phases, running sun and moon, and specified term; the HFT maps their roots and roles back to the focus. Because that mapping is legacy_unbound and context morphology is absent, the reading remains qualified and attributed.

findings.title: Crisis makes creaturely dependence experiential
findings.claim: The focus's needlessness and sufficiency meet 31:32's storm scene as an experiential contrast: people cannot secure themselves under the waves, invoke Allah alone, are rescued, and some later deny the signs, making dependence and its possible disavowal visible.
findings.mechanism: Al-Ghaniyy carries independence from need and a related capacity to suffice; 31:32 separately presents an enclosing disturbance, exclusive invocation, rescue to land, and post-rescue denial. Their contact makes divine independence more than an abstract contrast with creation: the context shows creaturely reliance becoming explicit under pressure and then being covered over after safety.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees both the moment dependence surfaces and the later possibility that a rescued person can deny the signs that made it visible.
findings.containment: The storm is a contrastive disclosure, not a direct lexical gloss of al-Ghaniyy; it does not say that every person remains sincere after rescue. Its root, word-index, and role mappings remain attributed to the legacy_unbound HFT trace.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and storm-scene Arabic are supplied and the HFT trace names the contextual roles and focus return, but the reading is an explicitly contrastive, multi-step inference from an unbound source; exploratory records that reach without ranking it below other findings.

findings.title: A concrete favor gives praise a face of gratitude
findings.claim: The focus's al-Hamid remains the intrinsically praiseworthy one, while 31:31's ships moving by Allah's favor and its grateful response make the extension of praise as thanksgiving newly perceptible.
findings.mechanism: The focus word al-Hamid carries praiseworthiness, and the registered praise branch includes thanks for a good received. The independent pericope scene says ships travel by Allah's favor and names the patient and grateful as people for whom the sign is legible. That concrete favor contacts the praise facet, so the focus's predicate can be heard as praise that has an experienced ground for gratitude.
findings.reader_payoff: Praise at the focus becomes more than an abstract quality: the nearby ship scene lets the reader see a concrete favor to which gratitude responds.
findings.containment: The word remains a predicate of intrinsic praiseworthiness; gratitude is a contextual extension, not a replacement or a claim that every praise is thanks. The connection row is a nomination, and target morphology for 31:31 is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The registered focus branch and exact 31:31 surface directly support the favor-to-gratitude contact. The connection row only nominates the relation and supplies no target morphology, so the contextually inferred extension is marked qualified.
